Disease of capillaries, which are blood vessels; no additional organ applies across the umbrella.
Proline metabolism defect; developmental disability and seizures common in annotated cohorts; nephropathy frequent (30-79%), despite often benign presentation.
Sweat gland carcinoma arising in dermis and infiltrating subcutis; uncommon site-specific subtypes do not define the umbrella.
Familial cortical myoclonic tremor and epilepsy are neurologic disorders, even when overt seizures are infrequent.
Inherited right ventricular cardiomyopathy with ventricular arrhythmias and structural cardiac disease.
EYS-related retinal degeneration causes progressive loss of retinal function and vision.

Inborn immune deficiency defined by inflammatory bowel disease and recurrent infections of the sinuses and lungs.
Congenital fusion of humerus and radius defines the disorder; renal insufficiency and external ear anomalies lack frequencies supporting additional axes.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure with elevated gonadotropins; gonadal hormone failure belongs to the endocrine axis.
Lung parenchymal inflammation and fibrosis define this heterogeneous group; an immune mechanism does not apply throughout.
Immune-mediated drug hypersensitivity; transient eruptions and variable organ-specific reactions do not establish common lasting organ damage.
Bone marrow failure and pulmonary fibrosis are core telomere disease manifestations; hepatic and cutaneous disease vary across subtypes without a reliable umbrella frequency >=30%.
Inflammatory optic neuropathy, usually immune-mediated demyelination; the optic nerve is assigned to ocular. Associated CNS diseases are separate diagnoses.
Infection of neonatal breast tissue; breast has no anatomical axis, but the infectious mechanism applies.
Parasites occupy skin and subcutis, causing nodules and chronic dermatitis; damaging ocular disease varies geographically and is not reliably >=30% across all infections.
Occlusion of a retinal venous branch is both an ocular disorder and a vascular occlusive disease.
Benign neoplasms of female reproductive organs; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ is intrinsic to this umbrella.
Stippled cartilage calcification and skeletal dysplasia define the group; intellectual disability, ichthyosis and ocular disease vary substantially by subtype.
ILD and developmental brain disease define it; hepatic steatosis and pituitary/thyroid failure each 1/1; skeletal abnormalities and anemia omitted by the four-axis cap.
Auditory-pigmentary syndrome: sensorineural hearing loss 12/14 and characteristic hair/skin pigmentation changes; heterochromia alone does not impair ocular function.
Microcephaly and congenital arthrogryposis each 5/5; microphthalmia is occasional (5-29%) in this subtype, and photosensitivity lacks a supporting frequency.
